notes.front: What is an application programming interface (API)?
notes.back: A set of rules and definitions through which separate pieces of software connect and swap data.
notes.explanation: The study guide adds that it acts as a standard translation layer, so that communication between systems is predictable and secure.
notes.example: Like a restaurant menu and order slip: diners get food without entering the kitchen, but they can only order what the menu offers.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Modernize Infrastructure and Applications with Google Cloud”, p. 10
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.back: Google Cloud's native API management platform, used to build, manage and secure APIs for any use case, environment or scale.
notes.explanation: It does this through high-performance API proxies that give backend services a consistent, reliable interface.
notes.example: Like a hotel reception desk: guests deal only with reception, but staff can rearrange the rooms behind it without guests noticing.
notes.evidence: Apigee is Google Cloud's native API management platform that can be used to build, manage, and secure APIs — for any use case, environment, or scale. Apigee offers high performance API proxies to create a consistent, reliable interface for your backend services.

notes.front: According to the exam guide, how can organisations create new business opportunities with APIs?
notes.back: By exposing public-facing APIs and monetising them.
notes.explanation: The exam guide lists this beside defining an API and the business value of Apigee, as one part of the business value of APIs.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader exam guide (August 2026), p. 5
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Apigee's monetisation feature let an API provider do?
notes.back: Add a rate plan to an API product, which lets it charge developers for using its APIs and so earn revenue from them.
notes.explanation: The rate plan is what turns API use into revenue: it lets the provider charge developers whenever the APIs are used.
notes.source: Overview of Apigee monetization, “Monetize your APIs using Apigee monetization”
notes.evidence: As an API provider, you need an easy-to-use and flexible way to monetize your APIs so that you can generate revenue whenever your APIs are used. Using Apigee's monetization feature, you can add a rate plan to an API product. The rate plan lets you charge the developers for using your APIs.

notes.front: Why is security a challenge for API producers?
notes.back: Their services are made available over the web, so they must protect them from unauthorised access.
notes.explanation: The documentation lists security first among the challenges producers face when exposing backend services.
notes.source: What is Apigee?, “Challenges for API producers”
notes.evidence: Security: Because API producers make their services available over the web, they must take all necessary steps to secure and protect their services from unauthorized access.

notes.front: Why can backend services stay unchanged when Apigee adds security or traffic rules to an API?
notes.back: The policies and actions are implemented on Apigee, in its API proxy layer, not in the backend services.
notes.explanation: Features are added at the proxy, which sits in front of the backend, so nothing behind it needs to change.
notes.source: What is Apigee?, “What does Apigee provide?”
notes.evidence: Because the policies and actions are implemented on Apigee, in the API proxy layer, your underlying backend services can remain unchanged.

notes.front: In the study guide's list of what Apigee does for an organisation, which item is about keeping APIs safe?
notes.back: It helps organisations secure their APIs.
notes.explanation: The study guide describes Apigee as operating APIs with enhanced scale, security and automation; this item is the security part.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Modernize Infrastructure and Applications with Google Cloud”, p. 10
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the study guide's list of what Apigee does for an organisation, which item tells a business how its APIs are being used?
notes.back: It tracks and analyses API usage.
notes.explanation: The study guide lists tracking and analysing usage beside securing, developing and deploying APIs.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Modernize Infrastructure and Applications with Google Cloud”, p. 10
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the study guide's list of what Apigee does for an organisation, which item supports teams building and releasing APIs?
notes.back: It helps with developing and deploying APIs.
notes.explanation: Apigee covers the build side of an API as well as its protection and measurement.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Modernize Infrastructure and Applications with Google Cloud”, p. 10
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which three API features does the study guide say Apigee offers?
notes.back: API versioning, API documentation and API throttling.
notes.explanation: The study guide lists these three features alongside securing, tracking and developing APIs.
notes.source: Cloud Digital Leader study guide, “Modernize Infrastructure and Applications with Google Cloud”, p. 10
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Apigee offer API producers under the heading of API insights?
notes.back: Security, monitoring and analytics features to secure access, monitor uptime and traffic with alerting, and see how the APIs are used.
notes.explanation: All three serve API producers: controlling access, watching uptime and traffic, and understanding how the APIs are used.
notes.evidence: Apigee offers Advanced API security, API monitoring, and analytics features that enable API producers to secure access to their services, monitor uptime and traffic with alerting, and gain insight into how their APIs are being used.

notes.front: A weather-data company finds one partner's app calling its API thousands of times a second, slowing the service for everyone else. Which Apigee control deals with this directly?
notes.back: D) Rate limiting and quotas in its API proxy layer
notes.choices:
A) API documentation
B) API versioning
C) A developer portal
D) Rate limiting and quotas in its API proxy layer
notes.choicesExplained: A) API documentation helps developers understand the API; it does not limit calls. B) API versioning manages changes between versions of an API. C) A developer portal helps developers find and register for APIs, not limit their traffic.
notes.explanation: Apigee's proxy layer gives granular control over rate limiting and quotas for all of your services.
notes.evidence: The proxy layer gives you granular control over security, rate limiting, quotas, analytics, and more for all of your services.

notes.front: A logistics firm has built a parcel-tracking API that online shops want to use, and it wants to charge the shops each time they use it. What should it set up in Apigee?
notes.back: A) Monetisation, with a rate plan on an API product
notes.choices:
A) Monetisation, with a rate plan on an API product
B) API versioning
C) An extra backend service for each shop
D) A developer portal only
notes.choicesExplained: D) A developer portal helps developers find and use the API but does not charge them. B) Versioning manages change, not billing. C) Extra backend services do not bill anyone; charging is set up in Apigee.
notes.explanation: A rate plan on an API product lets the provider charge developers for using its APIs, generating revenue whenever they are used.
notes.source: Overview of Apigee monetization, “Monetize your APIs using Apigee monetization”
notes.evidence: Using Apigee's monetization feature, you can add a rate plan to an API product. The rate plan lets you charge the developers for using your APIs.

notes.front: A bank wants outside app developers to find its APIs, read the documentation needed to build on them, and register so they hear about changes. Which Apigee offering fits?
notes.choices:
A) A rate plan
B) API throttling
C) A developer-focused portal
D) Replacing the backend services
notes.choicesExplained: B) API throttling limits how often clients call; it does not help them find the APIs. A) A rate plan charges developers for use. D) Replacing the backend changes what sits behind the API, not how developers discover it.
notes.explanation: Apigee’s portal is where client app developers discover APIs, find their documentation and register to stay in sync with updates.
notes.evidence: Apigee offers API producers a developer-focused portal where client app developers can discover your APIs, find the documentation required to build applications using them, and register as an app developer to stay in sync with any updates or changes.

notes.front: An insurer must replace the database behind its quotes API, but the partner apps that call the API must keep working throughout. How does Apigee help?
notes.back: A) Its proxies isolate API consumers from the backend, so the backend can change while client apps carry on uninterrupted
notes.choices:
A) Its proxies isolate API consumers from the backend, so the backend can change while client apps carry on uninterrupted
B) It copies the database into every partner app
C) It requires every partner to rewrite its app for the new database
D) It pauses all API traffic until the change is finished
notes.choicesExplained: B) Apigee sits between clients and the backend; it does not copy data into client apps. C) The point of the proxy is that clients need not change. D) The documentation says clients carry on without interruption.
notes.explanation: This is the API reliability benefit the documentation describes for Apigee proxies.
notes.evidence: Using Apigee proxies allows you to isolate API consumers from your backend service. This means that you can make changes to your backend while allowing client applications to consume your services without interruption.

notes.front: In Apigee's terms, how do API producers differ from API consumers?
notes.back: Producers build and manage the APIs that expose their backend services; consumers use the API's data in their client applications.
notes.explanation: Apigee is designed to benefit both kinds of user, each with its own API management challenges.
notes.evidence: Apigee is designed to benefit two key types of users and the unique API management challenges they face: - API producers: API producers build and manage the APIs that expose their backend services. - API consumers: API consumers use the data provided by the API in their client applications.
